title: Thread pool starvation
sub: .Result, Thread.Sleep and why a thread shouldn't wait
cards/0/title: A waiting thread is a wasted thread
cards/0/body:
If code on the pool calls .Result, .Wait() or Thread.Sleep, the thread just sits there doing nothing while it waits for the network or disk.

Tie up every thread like that, and new tasks pile up in the queue. That's thread pool starvation.
cards/1/task: Add 16 requests that wait on the network via .Result and start the clock. See how many threads are stuck and how the pool grows.
cards/2/q: The pool keeps adding threads, but the queue still doesn't move. Why?
cards/2/options/0: The new threads also pick up .Result requests and start waiting too
cards/2/options/2: .Result requests run one at a time
cards/2/explain: As long as the code blocks the thread, every new thread just becomes one more waiter.
cards/3/body:
With await, the thread doesn't wait for the network: it sends the request and goes straight back to the pool for the next task.

When the response arrives, the continuation joins the queue and runs on any free thread.
cards/4/task: Compare: add 16 requests that use await and look at the thread count and the average wait.
cards/5/options/0: With await the same threads serve more requests: while the network wait is on, the thread is free
cards/5/options/1: await downloads data from the network faster
cards/5/options/2: await creates a new thread for every request
cards/5/explain: The network didn't get faster. The thread just works on other requests while there's no response yet.
cards/5/wrong/2: The opposite: await doesn't create threads. Waiting on the network doesn't occupy a thread at all.
cards/6/q: What can cause thread pool starvation? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: .Result and .Wait() on tasks doing network calls
cards/6/options/1: Thread.Sleep in code running on the pool
cards/6/options/2: A synchronous read from a slow disk in every request
cards/6/explain: Anything that holds a pool thread without doing work. await and short computations don't hold the thread.
cards/7/q: An ASP.NET Core server: under load, responses suddenly lag by seconds, yet the CPU is nearly idle. What do you suspect first?
cards/7/options/0: Thread pool starvation: blocking calls like .Result somewhere
cards/7/explain: An idle CPU with growing latency is the classic sign: the threads exist, but they're stuck waiting.
cards/8/body:
Threads, the pool and locking are the foundation of async/await. Next up: what the compiler does with await, where the code continues, and where the infamous .Result deadlock in UI apps comes from.

That's a separate course, "Async/await in depth". You'll find it in the catalog.
cards/8/deep: Since .NET 6 the pool compensates faster for blocking on Task.Wait and .Result by adding a thread right away. That eases the symptoms but doesn't cure them. A blocked thread still sits idle and eats memory, and under heavy load the compensation isn't enough.
